sourcePolicy: All questions in this pack are Ready2Go original draft practice items unless an individual record states otherwise. No official JAMB past-question corpus is included. Human subject-matter and answer-key review is required before public release.

questions.question: Which three colours are traditionally called primary colours in basic paint mixing?
questions.explanation: The traditional RYB model uses red, yellow and blue as primary pigments.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Mixing blue and yellow pigment traditionally produces which colour?
questions.explanation: Blue and yellow pigments commonly mix to green.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Linear perspective is used to create what illusion in a flat image?
questions.explanation: Perspective uses converging lines and scale to suggest depth.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Which art element describes how light or dark a colour appears?
questions.explanation: Value refers to relative lightness or darkness.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Texture in visual art describes what?

options.B: The age of the artist only

questions.explanation: Texture may be physical or visually implied.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A sculpture is primarily a work in which form?
questions.explanation: Sculpture occupies three-dimensional space.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The arrangement of visual elements in an artwork is called what?
questions.explanation: Composition is the organisation of elements in a work.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A pigment gives paint what?
questions.explanation: Pigments selectively absorb and reflect light, producing colour.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Colours opposite each other on a colour wheel are called what?
questions.explanation: Complementary colours sit opposite each other on a colour wheel.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A mark that moves through space and has length but little width is what?
questions.explanation: Line is a basic visual element.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Visual harmony is created when elements do what?

options.A: Must all be the same size
options.B: Work together in a coherent arrangement

questions.explanation: Harmony creates a sense of unity among visual elements.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Proportion concerns the relative size of what?

options.A: Parts of an artwork or objects
options.C: The cost of a brush only

questions.explanation: Proportion describes size relationships between parts.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Which process transfers an image from a prepared surface to another surface?
questions.explanation: Printmaking produces impressions from a plate, block or screen.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A mural is typically made on which surface?
questions.explanation: Murals are artworks made directly on walls or ceilings.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Watercolour paint is generally thinned with what?
questions.explanation: Water is the principal solvent for watercolour paint.
